_scenario: Two PhysicsWorlds — one "2d" on Rapier2dAdapter, one "3d" on Rapier3dAdapter, both with §32 sleeping off — tracked on ONE PhysicsSystem inside ONE Application, stepped 600 clean fixed frames of 1/60 s (10 s, exactly one fixed step each, nothing dropped). The "2d" world holds the examples/mechanism slider-crank: a motorised HingeJoint shaft at (-5.4, 0.6) driving a 0.85 m crank, a crank-pin hinge, a wrist-pin hinge, a SliderJoint carriage limited to ±0.95 m about the stroke centre x = -3, a SpringJoint (rest 3.4 m, k = 25 N/m, c = 0.8 N·s/m) to a static post at x = 0.4 — plus an independent RopeJoint load (maxLength 1.5 m) that starts slack. The "3d" world holds a motorised shaft hinged about +Y, a SphericalJoint pendulum pushed 1 N·s along +Z on step 1, and a 1 kg SliderJoint carriage (limits ±0.5 m, velocity motor) pulling on a SpringJoint to a post at x = 8. Scripted §28 reconfiguration at fixed steps: setMotor retarget on both shafts and a reversal of the 3D slider motor on step 120; setLimits on both sliders on step 220 (2D widened to ±1.2, 3D tightened to ±0.3, i.e. inside the carriage's present travel); enableMotor(false) on both shafts on step 300; a 0.001 N·m·s kick on the released 3D shaft on step 340; enableMotor(true) on step 400; removeJoint on step 500 (the 2D rope and the 3D spring). Nothing in either world can touch anything: static bodies carry no collider, jointed pairs have §28 collision disabled, and every other body is out of reach — so the §29 tallies below are all zero by construction and are recorded as the measurement of that claim. The per-step digest is the D6 FNV-1a hash of the pair (world2d.checksum(), world3d.checksum()) in that order — §33's own checksums are the digest inputs, not a re-derivation — and summaryDigest is the same hasher over all 600 per-step digests in step order. Every "Micro" field is an integer count of 1e-6 units: micrometres for a travel or a position, micro-radians per second for a rate.
_tier: same-runtime (§33). Rapier is compiled WebAssembly, so its arithmetic does not vary with the host JS engine's Math library — but cross-platform determinism is NOT claimed here: values cross the JS/wasm boundary as f64 → f32, the wasm image is pinned per platform by the package manager, and §33's cross-platform tier requires evidence this suite does not gather. The checksum algorithm itself is exact and cross-platform; only its inputs are runtime-bound.
